desc:
CRM setup for small sales teams turns a blank or default account into a system that follows how you sell. Ecom Swift LLC configures custom fields, users, permissions, layouts and settings, and hands over a short guide with screenshots.

## What does a CRM setup include?

A CRM setup is the configuration work done after you subscribe and before your team starts relying on the tool. It covers the details you track on a contact or company, the people who can log in and what each one may see, how records look on screen and basic account settings such as time zone, currency and notifications.

Without it, you get the default account, built for an average business that does not exist. With it, the CRM speaks your language from the first day.

## Why default settings slow a team down

Out of the box, a CRM asks for fields you will never use and lacks the ones you need. Salespeople scroll through clutter to find a phone number. Someone stores the lead source in the notes because there is no field for it, and now it cannot be reported on. Every user is an administrator because nobody had time to set roles, so one wrong click can change settings for everyone.

These small frictions add up. People enter less data, enter it inconsistently or go back to their own notebooks. A tidy setup makes the right behavior the easy behavior.

## How a good setup affects day-to-day selling

Once the account matches your process, entering a lead takes seconds and the information is consistent. Required fields make sure the details you need, such as source or product interest, are captured every time. Layouts put the most useful facts at the top of a record, so a call can start with context rather than a search.

Roles and permissions protect your data. A new hire sees what they need and cannot delete the whole customer list. Saved views give each person a ready-made list, such as their open deals or leads waiting for contact. Later steps like pipelines, reminders and reports all depend on this foundation being right.

## What a properly configured CRM includes

- User accounts for everyone who needs one, each with a suitable role.
- Permissions that separate administrators, managers and regular users.
- Custom fields for the details your business tracks, with sensible types such as dropdowns or dates.
- Clean contact and company layouts that show the important fields first.
- Time zone, currency, date format and notification settings.
- A web form connected to the CRM, so enquiries arrive as records.
- Tags or labels for grouping contacts the way you speak about them.
- Saved views for each team member.
- A handover guide with screenshots that shows where everything is and how to enter a lead.

## How we do the work

We begin with a short conversation about your sales process, what you want to see on a contact and who needs access. From that we draft a field list and a user plan for your approval. Fields are easier to add than to remove, so we agree on them before building.

Then we configure the account, test it by entering sample leads the way your team would and adjust anything that feels clumsy. The Basic package covers users, a first set of fields, layouts and core settings. Standard adds roles, more fields, a connected web form and the handover guide. Premium covers larger teams, saved views, tags and an initial import of contacts, with a short period for small fixes afterward.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Track only the details you will actually use.
- Give each user the lowest permission level that lets them do their job.
- Use dropdowns instead of free text wherever you want to report later.
- Write down who is responsible for the account settings.
- Keep the handover guide up to date.

**Avoid:**
- Creating a field for every idea anyone has had.
- Making every user an administrator.
- Leaving default fields in place that confuse the team.
- Importing data before the fields exist.
- Changing field types after thousands of records are filled in.

## Who this service is for

It suits a business that has just chosen a CRM and wants to start properly. It suits a team that has used a CRM casually for months and feels it never quite fits. And it suits an owner who is hiring salespeople and needs a consistent way for them to record leads.

## What we need from you

Tell us how you sell, what you want recorded on every lead and who needs to log in. Add us to your CRM as an admin or similar user where your plan allows it. We never need your password. You pay for your CRM plan directly to the provider, and our price covers the setup work only. If you have not chosen a CRM yet, our selection service helps you decide first.
